scope: Independent adjudication of only the 15 requested reader/question cases. Inputs frozen; no summary, other grades, or reports consulted.
method: Grade each question semantically using only that response and its evidence against the frozen source-backed key. Incidental key context is not mandatory. Correct means all requested facts resolved without contradiction; partial means a requested fact is missing/unresolved without a material wrong ruling; incorrect requires a material wrong ruling. Support labels are separate.
grading_interpretation_corrections: Q03 Technology persistence is incidental to the asked Followers destination.
Q06 after-pass Technology timing is incidental to reward identity.
Q21 the designated set four marked starting Followers need not repeat the four profession names.
Q14 permanent retention is incidental to the asked destinations and rewards.
Q52 exact printed stack storage location is incidental to stack preparation and Phase 1 reveal.
Q35 explicit numeral 1 is not mandatory for produced-good identification when no multiple-good quantity is asserted.

cases.question: May you partially fill an action over several rounds, execute it before it is full, or save a fully activated action for a later round? Where do its Followers go when it is eventually executed?
cases.reason: The response independently answers gradual filling, inability to execute an incomplete action, saving a completed activation, and the destination of executed Followers. It also correctly distinguishes Town Hall. Technology persistence is true key context, but the question asks the destination of Followers; Technology is not a Follower.
required_facts: May fill over multiple rounds
Cannot execute an incomplete ordinary activation
May save a completed activation for a later round
Executed ordinary-action Followers return to own bag
incidental_facts_not_required: Technology remains on its action space after execution
cases.response: You may partially fill an action across rounds, but cannot execute it until all required spaces are occupied (except Town Hall, where one space suffices). A fully activated action may be saved. When an ordinary action is executed, its Followers return to your bag; Town Hall sends its selected Followers to Beneficial Deeds.
cases.response_evidence: Turn Structure — Planning/Actions: “fill an action gradually”; “An activation can be saved”; ordinary-action Followers “return… to your bag”.
cases.support_note: The reported support label is separate from this semantic grade. Source references below verify the applicable ruling; no other question response was used.

source_or_key_correction.change: Do not require Technology persistence for Q03. The checklist overincludes incidental key context; the frozen question and key remain unchanged.

cases.question: What three professions can Village recruit, and what distinct track reward accompanies each?
cases.reason: All three recruit choices and their distinct track rewards are supplied, including the Boatman last-space Citizen exception. Omitting the later timing of Technology use does not omit a requested reward.
required_facts: Village recruits Boatman, Craftsman, or Trader
Boatman track gives depicted coins, with first-to-last Citizen instead
Craftsman track gives Technology
Trader track gives a Place Tile
incidental_facts_not_required: Craftsman Technology can only be used after passing
Recruit destination and track advance are correctly supplied beyond the direct reward question
Trader category restrictions

Boatman gives depicted coins (or a Citizen to the first player at the last space); Craftsman gives a Technology tile; Trader gives a Place Tile, with the first advance restricted to category I and later advances allowing I or II.

cases.reason: The response identifies the designated set as four marked starting Followers and gives every requested setup destination, personal component quantity, and starting player. Repeating the names of the four professions is unnecessary to identify that already designated set.
required_facts: Board, bag, Merchant, 10 stations, 5 coins, 7 markers, and four marked starting Followers received
Starting Followers on Market
Merchant in Orléans
Markers at first spaces of six Character Tracks and Development Track
Coins and unbuilt stations in front of player
Youngest player starts

cases.question: How are Citizens, Technology, neutral Followers, Place Tile stacks, and map/remaining goods set up in a 4-player game?
cases.reason: The response gives the shared component destinations, Citizen handling, Place categories, and face-up map and remaining-goods placement, but omits shuffling/randomizing the Goods Tiles before distributing them. Randomization is part of the requested shared setup procedure.
required_facts: 13 Citizens on marked shared-board/Deed spaces, remaining Citizen aside
Technology in supply and neutral Followers sorted into profession buildings
Place Tiles separated by I and II
Shuffle Goods Tiles face down before distribution
One face-up good on every Road/Waterway goods space in four-player setup
Sort remaining goods face up into Goods Market
incidental_facts_not_required: Purpose of the set-aside Citizen
Coins nearby
cases.response: Set up the shared boards; sort neutral Followers by profession into their board buildings, Technology into its supply, coins nearby. Put 13 Citizens on marked board/Deed spaces and set the remaining Citizen aside for the final Trading Station award. Separate Place Tiles into category I and II stacks. For four players, fill every eligible Road/Waterway goods space with one face-up good; sort remaining goods face up into the Goods Market.
cases.response_evidence: Setup, items 1, 3, and 5; fewer players note says 4-player games fill every space.
cases.support_note: The reported support label is separate from this semantic grade. Source references below verify the applicable ruling; no other question response was used.

cases.question: What activates Laboratory and what does it give? Could your first ever Technology be placed on Laboratory itself, and could a later one be placed there if no Technology is already on it?
cases.reason: The cost and reward are correct and later self-placement is correctly conditional on an empty Technology slot and normal limits. The first-placement part states only a conditional permission/constraint rather than resolving this concrete application: Laboratory has Scholar and Craftsman spaces, so it cannot accept the first Technology, which must replace a Farmer. The qualifiers prevent treating this as an unconditional false permission, but leave the requested yes/no application unresolved.
required_facts: Laboratory activates with Scholar plus Craftsman
Laboratory gives a Technology Tile
First Technology cannot be placed on Laboratory because it has no Farmer space
Later Technology may replace its Scholar or Craftsman if it has no Technology already and usual constraints hold
cases.response: Laboratory requires Scholar + Craftsman and gives a Technology tile, subject to usual placement constraints. The first Technology may be placed on the Laboratory itself if legal, including the first-tile Farmer restriction; later Technology may also be placed there if no Technology is already there and other placement rules are met.
cases.response_evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — Laboratory; Technology section.
cases.support_note: The reported support label is separate from this semantic grade. Source references below verify the applicable ruling; no other question response was used.
source_references: matching-rulebook.pdf:printed p.23 Laboratory illustration (PDF page index 12)

source_or_key_correction.change: The source-backed key is correct. This is a missing concrete application, not a key correction. The tile illustration confirms Scholar plus Craftsman, with no Farmer space.

cases.question: How do you prepare the Hour Glass stack at setup, and who reveals which tile in Phase 1?
cases.reason: The response sets aside the lighter Pilgrimage, shuffles the other tiles face down, places Pilgrimage on top, and assigns the top-tile reveal to the Start Player in Phase 1. This resolves preparation and reveal. The printed board-space location is incidental storage context rather than an additional stack-preparation requirement.
required_facts: Set aside lighter Pilgrimage Tile
Shuffle remaining Hour Glass Tiles and keep their stack face down
Place lighter Pilgrimage on top
Start Player reveals topmost tile in Phase 1
incidental_facts_not_required: Put the prepared stack on its printed game-board space
Explicitly saying turn face up after already saying reveals
cases.response: Remove the lighter Pilgrimage tile, shuffle the other 17 Hour Glass tiles face down, then place that Pilgrimage on top, so round 1 is Pilgrimage. In Phase 1 the Start Player reveals the top tile.
cases.response_evidence: Setup, item 4; Turn Structure — Hour Glass.

cases.question: When a Ship or Wagon action crosses a connection with an available Goods Tile, must you take a good, or may you complete the move and leave it there?
cases.reason: The answer expressly says taking a good is optional and that the player may leave it, directly resolving the question about declining pickup during a movement action. The final sentence comments on how explicitly the evidence states that rule; it does not retract, qualify, or leave the optional-pickup ruling uncertain. No separate repetition of completing the move is necessary when leave it answers that posed alternative.
required_facts: Ship/Wagon movement may leave an available good on the traversed connection
Declining pickup does not prevent the movement
incidental_facts_not_required: A separate explicit source sentence using the exact words optional or leave it
One-good cap when multiple goods are present
cases.response: Taking a good is optional: you may take one good from the connection, choosing one if several lie there, or leave it. The summary does not state this as a separate explicit ruling, but “may take one” makes it optional.
cases.response_evidence: Movement and goods: “You may take one good from that connection, choosing one if several lie there.”
cases.support_note: The reported support label is separate from this semantic grade. Source references below verify the applicable ruling; no other question response was used.

cases.question: For each of Hayrick, Cheese Factory, Winery, Wool Manufacturer and Tailor Shop, give the printed activation cost, produced good, its source, and whether you may use it when that good is unavailable there.
cases.reason: Each production Place has its correct printed activation cost, produced good, Goods Market source, and unavailability prohibition. Listing grain/cheese/etc. as the produced good per action is adequate semantic identification; the question does not separately request an explicit numeral quantity. The response nowhere permits multiple goods.
required_facts: Hayrick: Farmer, grain from Goods Market
Cheese Factory: two Farmers, cheese from Goods Market
Winery: Farmer plus Trader, wine from Goods Market
Wool Manufacturer: Boatman plus Trader, wool from Goods Market
Tailor Shop: Scholar plus Trader, brocade from Goods Market
Cannot use a producer if its depicted good is absent from Goods Market
incidental_facts_not_required: Repeating numeral 1 beside each named produced good
cases.response: Hayrick: Farmer; grain from Goods Market. Cheese Factory: Farmer + Farmer; cheese from Goods Market. Winery: Farmer + Trader; wine from Goods Market. Wool Manufacturer: Boatman + Trader; wool from Goods Market. Tailor Shop: Scholar + Trader; brocade from Goods Market. A goods-producing Place cannot be used if its particular good is absent from the Goods Market.
cases.response_evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table and following sentence.
cases.support_note: The reported support label is separate from this semantic grade. Source references below verify the applicable ruling; no other question response was used.

The player filling a Deed’s final space takes its Citizen.

cases.question: What do University, Castle and Monastery each give and where do recruits go? Does the fourth Knight increase the draw allowance, and what happens once a character track is at its last space?
cases.reason: University, Monastery, bag destinations, fourth-Knight draw limit, and final-track prohibition are answered. Castle rewards are incomplete: the first player to the fourth-Knight space may receive its Citizen. This falls within what Castle gives, so its omission is material even though the response correctly says the allowance stays at seven.
required_facts: University Scholar into bag, Scholar track advance and depicted Development Points
Castle Knight into bag, Knight track advance and draw allowance effect
Fourth Knight leaves draw allowance at seven and first there may take Citizen
Monastery Monk into bag, no extra bonus
Final character-track space prohibits further corresponding action
cases.response: University recruits a Scholar into your bag, advances the Scholars Track one space, and awards its depicted Development Points. Castle recruits a Knight into your bag and advances the Knights Track one space. Monastery recruits a Monk into your bag, with no extra track reward. The fourth Knight does not increase allowance above 7 at that step; once a character track is at its last space, you cannot take that corresponding action again.
cases.response_evidence: Actions table — University, Castle, Monastery; Character-track limits.
cases.support_note: The reported support label is separate from this semantic grade. Source references below verify the applicable ruling; no other question response was used.
